Given the integral $I = \iint_R xy(x + y) dx dy$ over the region bounded by $x = 0$, $y = 0$, and $x + y = 1$. The region $R$ is a triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, and $(0,1)$. The limits of integration are $x$ from $0$ to $1$, and $y$ from $0$ to $1 - x$. 

$I = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-x} (x^2y + xy^2) dy dx$. 

First, integrate with respect to $y$: 
$\int_{0}^{1-x} (x^2y + xy^2) dy = \left[ x^2  rac{y^2}{2} + x  rac{y^3}{3} ight]_0^{1-x} =  rac{x^2(1-x)^2}{2} +  rac{x(1-x)^3}{3}$. 

Factor out $x(1-x)^2$: 
$= x(1-x)^2 \left[  rac{x}{2} +  rac{1-x}{3} ight] = x(1-x)^2 \left[  rac{3x + 2 - 2x}{6} ight] =  rac{1}{6} x(1-x)^2 (x + 2)$. 

Now, integrate with respect to $x$ from $0$ to $1$: 
Let $1-x = t \implies dx = -dt$. When $x=0, t=1$; when $x=1, t=0$. 
$I =  rac{1}{6} \int_{1}^{0} (1-t) t^2 (3-t) (-dt) =  rac{1}{6} \int_{0}^{1} (3t^2 - 4t^3 + t^4) dt$. 
$=  rac{1}{6} \left[ t^3 - t^4 +  rac{t^5}{5} ight]_0^1 =  rac{1}{6} \left( 1 - 1 +  rac{1}{5} ight) =  rac{1}{30}$.
